content.title: Goodwill confirms all locations will close down for 24 hours leaving Walmart to scoop up business
content.text: GOODWILL has confirmed that all of its locations will close down for 24 hours, with Walmart left to scoop up the business. The popular thrifting store is following many other big name chains, but it will leave shoppers in the lurch for a whole day. Sign up for the Money newsletter Thank you! Goodwill has confirmed that all of its locations will close down for 24 hours, with Walmart left to scoop up the businessCredit: Getty As is customary for many retailers, Goodwill is closing to observe Easter Sunday. The holiday is very close, and millions of Americans have already secured their candy for the day. Goodwill is closing for Easter Sunday, which this year falls on April 20. The Goodwill site has confirmed the news, and usually closes for other major days like New Years, Thanksgiving and Christmas. The website says: “Goodwill stores typically close on Easter Day, as a major observed by many, Easter is one of the days Goodwill allows its employees to take off, ensuring they have time to spend with family and participate in holiday traditions. “Unlike standard business holidays such as New Year’s Day or Thanksgiving, Easter is not universally observed in the retail store, but Goodwill generally chooses to close its doors on this day. “However, it’s important to note that Goodwill locations are operated by independent local organizations, so policies can vary slightly from one region to another. “While the majority of stores follow the practice of closing on easter, some locations may have different holiday schedules based on community needs or operational preferences.” Most read in Money It is important to note that Goodwill operations are decentralized. Other stores that will be closed that day include: Best Buy Dick’s Sporting Goods Hobby Lobby Homesense Kohl’s Lowe’s Macy’s Sierra WHAT ELSE IS CLOSED ON EASTER SUNDAY? Some big name grocery options will also be closing for Easter Sunday, including Costco, Target, Aldi and Sam’s Club. The US Sun reported the news recently, meaning that shoppers looking for some last minute bits at the weekend will have to go elsewhere. A spokesperson for Target said of the temporary shutdown: “Guests can expect regular store hours on April 19 and can check Target.com or the Target app for local store information.” But never fear, because Walmart is still here to pick up the pieces. The major retailer will be one of the largest names still standing come Sunday, meaning it will rake up a lot of extra business. There’s also plenty of fast food options to enjoy on the big day, The US Sun revealed. These include McDonald’s, Pizza Hut and Starbucks. Some stores may be running limited hours, so it is always important to check with your local branch online first.
